subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stood still, mouth open, as the sun turned the tunnel mouth amber and gold.
source_quote: The sun. I keep coming back to that first moment of it — the way it hit the stone around the tunnel mouth and turned everything amber and gold, and I just stood there like an idiot with my mouth open.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer radiated warmth like a hearth, having endured months of darkness and now experiencing open sky and moving sun.
source_quote: Dawnbringer, at least, had no such ambivalence. I'd been aware of the sword's mood for days. It radiated warmth the way a hearth does — not directed at anything in particular, just present.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum turned his face up like he was receiving a blessing from the sun.
source_quote: Grygum turned his face up like he was receiving a blessing, which I suppose he was.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz squinted and pushed his spectacles up, calculating the precise angle of the light source.
source_quote: Daz squinted and pushed his spectacles up and looked like a man calculating the precise angle of the light source.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir went still in the particular way he goes still when something has moved him and he doesn't want anyone to notice.
source_quote: Zalthir went still in the particular way he goes still when something has moved him and he doesn't want anyone to notice.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool looked up at the sun, and his stillness was not his usual stillness — he was witnessing, not being a floor.
source_quote: Glabbagool just looked up. I don't know how an ooze looks at something. Technically. But those googly eyes caught the sun and he was absolutely, undeniably looking at it, and there was something in the stillness of him that wasn't his usual stillness. He wasn't being a floor. He was witnessing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir watched Glabbagool with the expression of a man reassessing a problem he thought he understood.
source_quote: Zalthir looked at Glabbagool with the expression of a man reassessing a problem he thought he understood.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was extremely stationary, moving the way continental shelves move.
source_quote: Glabbagool was, by most measurements, extremely stationary. He moved the way continental shelves move.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'He's got the stillness working for him,' noting Glabbagool's chief qualification for monk training.
source_quote: "He's got the stillness working for him," someone said — noting Glabbagool's chief qualification for the monk training Zalthir had apparently, in some sense, offered.

subject: Glabbagool's potential as a monk
fact: Glabbagool’s lack of fixed appendages and liquid form make his suitability for monk training uncertain and unverified.
source_quote: Whatever curriculum Zalthir had in mind — the run, run, slap, slap, slap that Glabbagool apparently had very strong feelings about — it would require some foundational work first.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'But he's unpredictable, because there are no fixed appendages,' recognizing Glabbagool's tactical threat.
source_quote: "But he's unpredictable," I said, "because there are no fixed appendages."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'It's easy to do, like, twelve hits in a round when you have twelve arms,' acknowledging Glabbagool's combat potential.
source_quote: "And it's easy to do, like, twelve hits in a round when you have twelve arms."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir asked whether he could become an ooze himself.
source_quote: Then Zalthir asked whether he could become an ooze himself.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir pivoted to whether Glabbagool could be equipped as a weapon.
source_quote: Then he pivoted to whether Glabbagool could be equipped as a weapon.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes weapons don't have agency — except his own.
source_quote: "It's not a weapon," I said. "Weapons don't have agency. Except mine."

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is perceived as a really cool sword who is kind of annoying sometimes, and she accepts this with the dignity of a master sculptor.
source_quote: Earlier, in fact, someone had described her as a really cool sword who was kind of annoying sometimes, which she had received approximately the way a master sculptor receives being called "pretty good with rocks."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'Look, you know, we got each other,' to Dawnbringer, and the hilt warmed slightly.
source_quote: "I'm annoying also, Dawnbringer," I said. "Look, you know, we got each other." The hilt warmed slightly.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth approached Thorin with the set of shoulders she gets when she's made a decision and is walking toward it rather than away from it.
source_quote: Eldeth found me a few minutes later, while the others were still adjusting to the light. She had that particular set to her shoulders she gets when she's made a decision and is walking toward it rather than away from it.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth calls Thorin 'giant friend' as part of his name now, not as mockery but as an earned term of respect.
source_quote: She uses that. Not as mockery — she stopped doing that somewhere in the deep dark... She says it like it's part of my name now.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth said, 'I swear,' promising to make Thorin's clan integration a statement of purpose after briefing the lords.
source_quote: And then: 'I swear.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'Alright, there we go,' in response to Eldeth's sworn oath, a simple but honest acknowledgment.
source_quote: "Alright," I said. "There we go."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wants to learn about his dwarven roots and become an integrated person — both his giant upbringing and his cultural roots.
source_quote: "I do want to learn about my dwarven roots. I want to become an integrated person — both my giant upbringing, but also my cultural roots, so, you know."

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth extended her hand and held it for a moment the way that means something more than a handshake.
source_quote: She extended her hand and I took it, and she held it for a moment the way that means something more than a handshake.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait announced, 'I'm just gonna go explore,' vibrating with the energy of someone about to make a terrible decision.
source_quote: "I'm just gonna go explore. It's totally safe for goblins, right? Nobody's gonna attack a goblin for being a goblin. We're totally integrated into the society."

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait asked if he could hang out with the group, seeking safety and inclusion.
source_quote: "Well, you know, I'm just a small goblin, and you're four big, powerful people. Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys? Maybe find a nice place? This Candlekeep place seems like the kind of place someone like me could find a job doing something innocuous."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir scanned the environment constantly, still habituated to the Underdark’s darkness even under open sky.
source_quote: The third day of open sky and I still hadn't stopped scanning. That's the thing about months underground: the habits don't switch off just because the ceiling lifts.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the northern treeline was wrong — no birds had moved, undergrowth didn’t shift with wind, indicating hidden presence.
source_quote: What I know now, without having been taught it properly, is that the trees north of us were wrong. Not visibly wrong. The wrongness was in the negative space — the way no birds had moved through that section for some time, the way the undergrowth hadn't shifted with the wind in quite the pattern it should.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum rolled his dice and concluded, 'You conclude that what is following you is a deer.'
source_quote: Grygum rolled his dice with the confidence of a man who already knows the answer. I watched him from the corner of my eye. He came up satisfied. "You conclude," came the word, "that what is following you is a deer."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin suggested Tremor Sense, forgetting they were no longer underground.
source_quote: Thorin raised the idea of Tremor Sense with the optimism of someone who'd forgotten which world we were currently standing on.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin complained, 'I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time... And then the one time I need it. We're not underground, and we're not surrounded by fucking stone.'
source_quote: "I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time," he said, with the conviction of a man delivering a formal complaint to the cosmos. "And I figured there would always be some stone. And then the one time I need it. We're not underground, and we're not surrounded by fucking stone."

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer told Thorin, 'You've got anger issues,' directly and without hesitation.
source_quote: "You've got anger issues," said Dawnbringer.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, 'The deer,' when the group realized the tracker was not a deer.
source_quote: "The deer," I said.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir corrected himself, 'Oh, no. It's not a deer. It's not a deer.'
source_quote: "Oh, no. It's not a deer. It's not a deer."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'Oh, dear,' after realizing the tracker was not a deer.
source_quote: "Oh, dear," said Grygum, somewhere behind me, apparently now awake.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin estimated the follower was twenty to forty feet away, likely closer to twenty.
source_quote: Twenty to forty feet, Thorin's read suggested. I adjusted my estimate of the gap. Closer to twenty.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed the follower was patient, not panicked, pacing rather than trailing.
source_quote: Whatever was in those trees had been moving with us, shifting position laterally to stay in the blind spots, using the terrain the way someone uses it when they know what they're doing. Not panicked. Not rushing. Patient. The kind of following that isn't trailing — it's pacing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted the follower had timed their approach to dusk — the worst possible window for visibility.
source_quote: Whoever was out there had timed this, or had simply been following us long enough to arrive at dusk by coincidence.

subject: Zalthir's training on environmental stillness
fact: Zalthir recalls a class about reading environmental stillness but cannot remember the instructor or the lesson, leaving the knowledge unverified.
source_quote: There was a class for this. I'm reasonably certain it was Brother Orveth — or possibly Brother Quellin... I remember the light in that room. I remember thinking I could be training instead. I don't remember what he said.

subject: Thorin's identity as a dwarf
fact: Thorin feels like a rock in the wrong place — too giant-raised for dwarven spaces, too dwarven for the hills — and his cultural integration remains unresolved.
source_quote: I'd spent most of my life not being the right kind of dwarf for any given room. Too giant-raised for dwarven spaces, too dwarven for the hills. There's a saying the old ones used — I'm translating badly — something like: a rock in the wrong place is just a rock.

subject: Glabbagool's agency
fact: Glabbagool’s capacity for witnessing and intention is observed but not formally understood or verified.
source_quote: I don't know how an ooze looks at something. Technically. But those googly eyes caught the sun and he was absolutely, undeniably looking at it, and there was something in the stillness of him that wasn't his usual stillness.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was not wrong about the stone, and his frustration was legitimate.
source_quote: He wasn't wrong about the stone. And his frustration was legitimate — he'd made a reasonable preparation for a reasonable environment, and we'd somehow ended up standing in the one terrain where it didn't apply.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to fireball the trees.
source_quote: Thorin's suggestion was to fireball the trees.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considered the suggestion to fireball the trees briefly.
source_quote: I considered this briefly, which is about as much time as it deserves.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was already thinking past the suggestion to fireball the trees.
source_quote: Daz was already thinking past it. I could see it in the way he'd gone still — not my kind of still, but a wizard's still, the kind where the mind is moving very fast and the body has just stopped participating.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said he wanted to get some intel out of this.
source_quote: "I want to get some intel out of this," he said, the way a man says a thing when he's already decided what he's going to do.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz announced he was going to misty step up into the tree.
source_quote: "I'm going to misty step up into the tree," Daz announced.

subject: Someone's speculation about Jimjar
fact: Someone speculated it might be Jimjar, coming to drag us back underground, and I did not rule it out.
source_quote: Someone speculated it might be Jimjar, coming to drag us back underground. I did not rule it out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum heard a bird call that was not a real bird — a cardinal's whistle, clean and bright, floating through tree cover that hadn't seen a cardinal in decades.
source_quote: The bird call came just as I was settling in for the night. Not a real bird — that was the point. A cardinal's whistle, clean and bright, floating through tree cover that hadn't seen a cardinal in decades, maybe ever.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the bird call was a successful imitation.
source_quote: Daz had been practicing. We all had, in the abstract, the way you talk about a plan more than you drill it. But hearing it land in the quiet of a forest evening, unmistakable against the rustle of leaves, I thought: *good. That actually worked.*

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool made an impression of a bird that was unrecognizable and entirely untrained.
source_quote: What followed it was Glabbagool, doing his best. His impression of a bird was everything you'd expect from a creature that has never encountered a bird, never encountered the concept of sound being produced intentionally for communication purposes, and was working from approximately zero reference points.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was very proud of his bird impression.
source_quote: He was very proud of it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool asked if the bird was a kind of ooze.
source_quote: "Is it a kind of ooze?" he asked, in that way he has, earnest and completely serious about the question.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum told Glabbagool that birds are feathered, not oozy.
source_quote: "No, no," I said, "they're not oozy at all. They're feathered."

subject: Glabbagool's understanding of feathers
fact: Glabbagool struggled to reconcile the concept of feathers with his understanding of creatures, and had no time to resolve it.
source_quote: The concept try to find somewhere to settle and fail to locate purchase. He didn't have three days. He had the next thirty seconds before we needed to move.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said he would introduce Glabbagool to real birds.
source_quote: "We'll introduce you," I said. "Yeah, yeah, I wander over there."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the divine plan had them covered, provisionally.
source_quote: The divine plan has us covered, in the broadest possible sense — or at least I choose to believe it does, provisionally, and correct the belief when the evidence demands it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the drow's movement from the north — careful, not panicked, close, twenty to forty feet.
source_quote: Thorin had picked up something in the terrain earlier — movement from the north, not panicked, not aggressive, careful. Close. Twenty, maybe forty feet.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum filed a mental note: drow on the surface, daylight hours, following quietly instead of attacking.
source_quote: The note I'd already filed, in my head: *drow, on the surface, daylight hours, following us quietly instead of attacking.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow was not a predator but a professional doing a job she'd rather not be doing.
source_quote: That combination doesn't say assassin to me. It says someone who got handed a bad assignment and is making the best of it. There's a difference between a predator and someone doing a job they'd rather not be doing, and I've learned to read that difference fast.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir ended the question of whether there would be a fight — there would not.
source_quote: By the time Glabbagool and I cleared the last of the underbrush, Zalthir had already ended the question of whether there would be a fight. There would not.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir grappled and stunned the drow spy with efficient finality.
source_quote: The spy — drow, slight, female, exactly as advertised — was grappled and stunned, held in place with the kind of efficient finality that Zalthir brings to everything he considers a problem worth solving immediately.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked who number two works for, in a voice with no subtlety.
source_quote: Thorin was standing over her, asking who number two works for, voice carrying through the trees with all the subtlety of a dwarf who was raised by hill giants and sees no reason to modulate volume as a social strategy.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said it was very rude to follow people without talking to them.
source_quote: "It's very rude," he said, which is the most Daz thing I've heard him say, possibly ever, "to follow people without just coming up and talking to them. So we'll talk to you now."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was calm and medical in his demeanor while tying up the drow.
source_quote: He said it while tying her up. The calm was so complete it was almost medical.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the drow was not watching the party but watching him, and working hard to hide it.
source_quote: She wasn't watching the party. She was watching me. And working very, very hard to make it look like she wasn't.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz asked why he was so important that she was trying hard not to make it look like she was following him.
source_quote: "So we may be able to figure something out where you live, but first you need to answer some questions. Why am I so important that you're trying hard not to make it look like you're following me, but you're following me?"

subject: Daz
fact: Daz admitted he had been away from home for a while, correcting his earlier statement about being drow.
source_quote: "Let me correct that. I've been away from home for a while."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz learned the matron mother of House T'sarran had ruled for two hundred years.
source_quote: She told us her matron had ruled House T'sarran for two hundred years.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized the drow were using him as bait to find the person who paid to have him protected.
source_quote: "My matron believes that the one who paid —" and here she pointed at me, with the resigned precision of someone who has run out of misdirection — "for him, will reveal themselves once he reaches the surface. We are looking for that person, not for you."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz concluded the drow were watching to report back what happened to him, so they could trace the person who paid for his protection.
source_quote: "So basically, you're treating me as bait. You're watching and observing so that when something happens to me, you can go report back what happened to me."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum asked the drow if she was looking for a new job.
source_quote: "Hey," he said, with the casual tone of someone considering a minor administrative matter, "are you looking for a new job? We could use another helper."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum handed the drow prayer beads without explanation or threat.
source_quote: Then Grygum held out the prayer beads. He didn't say anything particularly ominous. He just handed them to her and told her to put them on. No threat in his voice. No explanation of what they did.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum rolled persuasion and the drow talked.
source_quote: Then Grygum rolled persuasion, and she talked.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz learned the drow were sent to find where the party surfaced because their matron was waiting for them to surface.
source_quote: "I was just assigned to track you, not to engage. My orders were to report your surface destination, your contact, who approaches you."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz learned the drow's matron was looking for the person who paid to have him protected.
source_quote: "We are looking for that person, not for you."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz learned the matron cared because she cared — and therefore the drow cared.
source_quote: "The matron mother cares, and therefore I care."

subject: I
fact: I understood that I had been treated as bait — an indicator on the board moved to see who else responds.
source_quote: I understood what had just been said about me. Not Daz. Not even the wizard. The *indicator.* The piece on the board that you move to see who else moves in response. The bait.

subject: I
fact: I decided I'd give myself until we reached Candlekeep to develop the appropriate perspective on being used as bait.
source_quote: I thought about it for a moment and decided I'd give myself until we reached Candlekeep to develop the appropriate perspective.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of the drow's deal because it has no enforcement mechanism and she has no incentive to honor it beyond her own interest.
source_quote: I don't buy it. The minute she has the information she needs, she's off, and we get jack shit.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the only solution is to kill Daz to reveal who is protecting him.
source_quote: There's only one solution. We need to kill Daz.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considers killing Daz to be on the 'maybe list'.
source_quote: It's on the list. The maybe list.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum reassures the party that he has a Revivify spell, so Daz's death would be temporary.
source_quote: Oh, I have a Revivify spell.

subject: I
fact: I kept my expression neutral during the theoretical murder planning of Daz while a restrained enemy watched.
source_quote: I kept my expression neutral.

subject: I
fact: I have found purpose in being the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard and consider the current situation fine.
source_quote: I have found purpose. I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard. This is fine.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is relying on the prayer beads, not killing the drow, to achieve his goal.
source_quote: I'm not relying on killing you. I'm relying on the prayer beads.

subject: I
fact: I noticed Glabbagool walking with one eye permanently locked on the shrunken drow prisoner, and recognized the steadiness of his attention as the most earnest thing I'd seen in weeks.
source_quote: I noticed — not the spy's indignation, not Thorin's satisfaction, but Glabbagool, walking with one eye locked permanently on the prisoner. He had been assigned a job. He was doing the job. The care in it — the steadiness of that unblinking attention — was the most earnest thing I'd seen in weeks.

subject: I
fact: I realized I should have thought about what it would be like for Glabbagool to be carried in a bag with a furious, newly miniaturized assassin as his only company.
source_quote: I hadn't thought about what it would be like to be carried in a bag with a furious, newly miniaturized assassin as your only company. I should have thought about that.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considers shielding the shrunken drow from sunlight in the bag of holding to be mercy.
source_quote: This is mercy," Thorin confirmed.

subject: I
fact: I filed away Thorin's suggestion to nickname the shrunken drow 'Polly Pocket' as demeaning.
source_quote: Nickname her Polly Pocket," he said. Then, with the flat authority of someone who knows what he's doing: "It's very demeaning." I filed that away.

subject: I
fact: I understood that the drow woman had probably survived worse than being miniaturized and confined, but probably never anything quite like this.
source_quote: The drow woman inside had probably survived worse. But probably had never survived anything quite like this.

subject: I
fact: I thought about Asha Vandree and how she would have hated that her theological document would unlock questions in Candlekeep's library.
source_quote: I thought about Asha Vandree, briefly. The way she had looked through me the entire time we were in that room... She would have hated that.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is deeply confused by the concept of a library with finite questions attached to it.
source_quote: He wanted to know why we weren't simply donating every book we'd ever seen and asking questions until the end of time.

subject: I
fact: I was curious what Glabbagool would ask if given one question in Candlekeep, but did not say so.
source_quote: I was also curious what he'd ask. I didn't say so, but I thought about it for the better part of the road to Candlekeep...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum spent the road to Candlekeep turning over the same questions in his head about what Bahamut actually wants from him personally.
source_quote: I'd spent most of it turning the same questions over in my head like stones I kept expecting to find something under. What does Bahamut actually want from me? Not the general want... but the specific want. The personal assignment.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes therapy is a process, not a product, and that his needs cannot be resolved with a single question.
source_quote: Okay, but I mean, like, I'm looking for a therapist. This is not a one-question type of thing. This is — there are no shortcuts when it comes to therapy.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool told the spy he could poke her eyes out, then clarified that the googly eyes were just affectations and that he can see in different ways.
source_quote: He told the spy he could poke her eyes out, then immediately clarified — with the earnestness of someone who genuinely wants to be understood — that the googly eyes were just affectations. 'I can actually see different ways. This is how ooze work. But I discovered that if you have these cute eyes, people take you more friendly.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to grant a question, stating the listener did not donate a book.
source_quote: You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin received the description of Philemon as a man who had been hoping someone would say exactly those words.
source_quote: Thorin received this information like a man who has been hoping someone would say exactly these words.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that there were apparently two famous people in the party.
source_quote: Daz observed that there were apparently two famous people in the party.

subject: First Reader
fact: The First Reader assigned scholars, with Zalthir getting the Jimjar thread, which dovetailed with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.
source_quote: The First Reader assigned scholars. Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.

subject: Zalthir's Jimjar thread
fact: The Jimjar thread is unresolved and tied to an avowed named Khell-Vire whose specific interest remains unstated beyond being about 'me' in particular.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific. The First Reader clarified: not about the party generally, but about *me* in particular.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud beat Protanther at chess with an unexpected, definitive move that caused the world to shift.
source_quote: Stroud beat Protanther at chess. ... Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. The kind of thing that doesn't just work, it *announces* itself. Protanther was so stunned he joined the alliance. The world shifted because someone who didn't know what they were doing did the exact right thing at the exact right moment.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud's chess move became known as 'Stroud's Gambit,' a term that redefined a scholarly field.
source_quote: And then, because I couldn't help it, and because the phrase had been sitting in the back of my mind since we started this journey and I'd never had the right audience for it: 'Stroud's Gambit.'

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth expressed outrage at the First Reader for not informing him about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth has a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts, a previously quiet, small area of study.
source_quote: He had, he explained breathlessly, a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts. Which had, until recently, been a quiet, small area of study. A niche. Something he'd pursued with quiet dedication while the rest of the academic world found more fashionable problems.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth grabbed the speaker's hand and practically dragged them.
source_quote: He grabbed my hand and practically dragged me.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker let Vareth drag them because they were curious and had questions of their own.
source_quote: I let him. I was curious, and also I had questions of my own.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker believes it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to take over the world, but has not moved into that phase yet.
source_quote: You have to understand," I said, with the measured cadence I use when I'm testing someone, "that it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to try to take over the world. But I haven't moved into that phase yet.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is eager to test out theories about Bahamut half-orc conversions and is thrilled to receive new information.
source_quote: This is all fascinating! I have so many theories I wish to test out.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker completed Vareth's thought by saying, 'It truly was legendary.'
source_quote: I felt it coming together and finished the thought for him: 'It truly was legendary.'

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth reacted with surprise, recognition, and delight upon hearing the term 'Stroud's Gambit.'
source_quote: Vareth stopped. His expression went through several stages very quickly — surprise, recognition, something that looked almost like delight at receiving a gift he hadn't known he wanted. '*Oh.* Oh! Well, that's not how — this is all novel news! I can't wait to take advantage of it!'

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker said, 'It's all part of the plan,' in response to Vareth's enthusiasm.
source_quote: Oh," I said, as warmly as I could manage, "it's all part of the plan.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum's name was pulled into a discussion about Daz's habit of citing Malfire at every opportunity.
source_quote: Somewhere in the background, the rest of the party had begun debating Daz's habit of citing Malfire at every available opportunity. I heard Grygum's name pulled into the discussion — *Grygum*, not me, which is how I know the sentence was reconstructed after the fact

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker describes the party's dynamic as being sick of each other but still together.
